validity.recommendation: Adjudicate against P5521 (Belogorsk-Khabarovsk Gas Pipeline, Svobodny->Khabarovsk Territory, 828 km, status=construction). Both rows track the same physical corridor: a connector linking the Power of Siberia (Chayanda-sourced) system to the Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok (Sakhalin-sourced) system across Amur Oblast, the Jewish Autonomous Oblast, and Khabarovsk Krai. energypolicy.ru's 2024 academic account gives the actual history: a Belogorsk(Amur Oblast)-Birobidzhan(JAO)-Khabarovsk extension WAS part of Power of Siberia-1's ORIGINAL design (when PoS-1 was planned to run Chayanda->Vladivostok with an LNG plant there); it was 'set aside' ('otoshel na vtoroy plan') once Gazprom instead routed China-bound gas directly via Blagoveshchensk (the trunk actually built, 2019). That shelved concept is very likely what GEM staged as P3208 ('Phase I Expansion', Blagoveshchensk->Khabarovsk Krai, cancelled) -- existence and the 'cancelled' framing are independently corroborated (see status_reviews). BUT the SAME corridor has since 2022 been revived under the name 'MG Belogorsk-Khabarovsk' (830 km per energypolicy.ru, matching GEM's own P5521 at 828 km) as part of the 'Eastern Gas Supply System' (Vostochnaya sistema gazosnabzheniya / VSG), officially listed alongside Power of Siberia-2 in the Russian government's 16-Nov-2024 decree No. 3302-r (legalacts.ru) covering Gazprom's mandated trunk-pipeline construction program, target completion 2029 (prokhab.ru, eastrussia.ru, both Oct 2022). Recommendation: either (a) merge P3208 into P5521 if GEM intends one continuous project record (revived project inherits the corridor), or (b) if GEM's convention is to retain the original shelved 1st-generation concept as its own row, then P3208's segment name/notes should say explicitly that it is the PRE-2022 discontinued precursor to the corridor now tracked as P5521, so a researcher does not read the two rows as unrelated pipelines or double-count 620+828=1448 km of corridor that is physically one ~800-830 km route. Whichever way this is resolved, P3208's own LengthKnown/Capacity numbers (620 km / 32 bcm/y) are NOT supported by any source found for either the original or the revived concept -- see the spec concern below.
validity.researcher_notes: Read to exhaustion: prokhab.ru (Wayback, Oct 2022, Khabarovsk krai governor's press service), eastrussia.ru (Wayback, Oct 2022, same underlying announcement -- these two are ONE origin, both relaying the governor's press service), energypolicy.ru (independent academic journal article, 2024, a genuinely separate origin with its own historical analysis), and neftegaz.ru + legalacts.ru (Nov 2024, reporting/quoting the actual government decree -- a third independent origin, official record). All four together: 3 independent origins corroborating that (1) a Belogorsk/Amur Oblast-to-Khabarovsk connector was part of PoS-1's original routing and was shelved, and (2) the same corridor concept, ~830 km, is now an active government-mandated construction project named 'Belogorsk-Khabarovsk', which is what P5521 already tracks. Checked P5521 is not itself sourced from these same documents in the current sheet (P5521 carries no [ref] per the roster's MISSING_REF/MISSING_VALUE pattern implied by the batch calibration), so this is new evidence for that row too -- filed as a cross_row_lead.

validity.recommendation: Do not carry LengthKnown=620.00 km or Capacity=32.00 bcm/y forward without further sourcing; both are uncorroborated. Every independent source found for this corridor (whether describing the original PoS-1-era concept or the revived 2022-24 project) states approximately 800-830 km, not 620 km -- prokhab.ru and eastrussia.ru both say 800 km (Oct 2022 announcement), and energypolicy.ru's 2024 academic account gives 830 km for 'MG Belogorsk-Khabarovsk' specifically. No source states 620 km for any Blagoveshchensk/Belogorsk-Khabarovsk gas line, and no source states a 32 bcm/y capacity for this corridor (the only capacity figure found nearby is the unrelated 10 bcm/y Far Eastern Route target and P5521's own recorded 28 bcm/y, itself unsourced on the sheet).
validity.researcher_notes: Searched Russian-language coverage of this corridor across all 42 harvested citations plus the open web (Gazprom project pages, the 2022 and 2024 Gazprom annual-report citations already on the wiki page, neftegaz.ru, energypolicy.ru, prokhab.ru, eastrussia.ru, the Nov-2024 government decree text via legalacts.ru/neftegaz.ru). The 620 km / 32 bcm/y pair does not appear in any of them. It is possible this is a stale or unofficial early estimate for the pre-2012 original-design 'Chayanda-to-Vladivostok-via-Khabarovsk' concept (which would have been longer than the Belogorsk-Khabarovsk connector alone, since it also had to reach Vladivostok) that GEM's original researcher sourced from a document not in the current citation pool and that has since rotted -- or it may simply be a data-entry error. Flagging rather than silently carrying it forward as REFS_ADDED.

cross_row_leads.facts: New ~800 km connector pipeline to be built from Khabarovsk Krai to Amur Oblast (through the Jewish Autonomous Oblast), linking the Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok trunk with Power of Siberia into Russia's Unified Gas Supply System. Project name 'Eastern Gas Supply System' (Vostochnaya sistema gazosnabzheniya). Decision to build made by President Putin, April 2022. Technical customer: Gazprom Invest LLC; general designer: Gazprom Proektirovanie LLC, which began collecting survey/engineering data Oct 2022. Target completion: 2029.

Academic 2024 source names this project 'MG Belogorsk-Khabarovsk', length 830 km, route Belogorsk (Amur Oblast) -> Birobidzhan (Jewish AO) -> Khabarovsk. Purpose: connect Eastern Siberia/Far East gas systems and supply the Jewish Autonomous Oblast; may also serve as a backup route for the 10 bcm/y Far Eastern Route (P3895) contract with China if the Yuzhno-Kirinskoye field's subsea development (sanctioned, no Russian subsea-production tech yet) slips. Engineering surveys for linking PoS-1 and SKV were completed by 2024; construction was expected to begin 2024, completion target 2029, with Gazprom/Minenergo discussing acceleration.

Nov 19, 2024: Russian government decree No. 3302-r (16 Nov 2024) formally lists 'sistema MGP Vostochnaya sistema gazosnabzheniya (VSG)' -- comprising Power of Siberia-2 AND Belogorsk-Khabarovsk -- among 13 trunk-pipeline projects Gazprom is mandated to build/reconstruct. Confirms Belogorsk-Khabarovsk is an active, government-tracked construction project as of late 2024, not merely a proposal.

'MG Chayanda-border with PRC (first stage of MG Power of Siberia-1)': length 2200 km, diameter 1420 mm, working pressure 9.8 MPa, export capacity 38 bcm/y -- matches the sheet's recorded LengthKnown=2200/Capacity=38 exactly; adds a new sourced Pressure=9.8 MPa (currently blank per batch calibration).

'MG Kovykta-Chayanda (second stage of MG Power of Siberia-1)': length 800 km, diameter 1420 mm, working pressure 9.8 MPa -- matches the sheet's recorded LengthKnown=800 exactly; adds sourced Pressure=9.8 MPa (currently blank). Also: full-length operation (Kovykta gas flowing) confirmed from Dec 2022; 2023 throughput via the Kovykta-Chayanda section specifically was 5.4 bcm.

'MG Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok': route length 1837 km (sheet has 1822 -- small discrepancy worth checking), diameter 1220 mm, working pressure 9.8 MPa, first-launch-complex design capacity 5.5 bcm/y. Separately: planned expansion of SKV is stated to enable pumping 'up to 20 bcm/y' -- matches the sheet's recorded Capacity=20.00 as an expansion target, not the original 5.5 bcm/y first-stage figure. Useful for resolving which capacity figure (5.5 vs 20) the sheet's number represents.

Confirms the SKV second string, Komsomolsk-na-Amure to Khabarovsk, 391 km including redundant lines and underwater crossings (sheet has 390.8 -- near-exact match), completed December 2021. This is presented as a genuine capacity-expansion string of SKV, not a duplicate of P0758 -- supports treating P0758 and P2027 as two distinct, real physical strings.

'Far Eastern Route (MG Power of Siberia-3)': 10 bcm/y to China, resource base = Sakhalin-3 shelf fields (Kirinskoye, Yuzhno-Kirinskoye, Myginskoye) plus the existing SKV trunk to Primorsky Krai. 25-year supply contract signed with CNPC 2022; technical agreement fixing cross-border parameters also 2022; intergovernmental agreement on the border crossing (Ussuri/Wusuli river, near Dalnerechensk, Primorsky Krai, to Hulin, Heilongjiang) signed/ratified 2023. Design capacity originally targeted for 2025 is now expected 'at the latest' in 2027, due to sanctions on Yuzhno-Kirinskoye's subsea production technology (Russia lacks a domestic deepwater subsea production complex). Matches the sheet's recorded status=proposed and Capacity=10.00.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The recorded 'cancelled' status is directionally supported: energypolicy.ru's 2024 account is explicit that the original Belogorsk/Blagoveshchensk-Khabarovsk extension concept envisioned in PoS-1's first design was set aside once China-bound gas was instead routed directly via Blagoveshchensk (the trunk actually built and operating since Dec 2019). No source found reviving THIS SPECIFIC 620 km / 32 bcm/y concept. HOWEVER -- and this is the caveat the validity/duplicate concern is for -- the same physical corridor is very much alive again: prokhab.ru and eastrussia.ru (Oct 2022) report Gazprom Invest beginning design work on an ~800 km Amur Oblast-to-Khabarovsk connector (targeting 2029), and the Nov 2024 government decree (neftegaz.ru/legalacts.ru) formally mandates Gazprom to build 'Belogorsk-Khabarovsk' as part of the Eastern Gas Supply System -- which is what GEM already tracks separately as P5521 (status=construction). So 'confirm cancelled' is the right call for P3208 AS CURRENTLY SPECIFIED (this exact 620 km/32 bcm/y entity), but a human should decide whether P3208 ought to exist at all as a distinct row once P5521's overlap is resolved -- see the duplicate concern. Not proposing a status change here because the revival is not evidence that THIS row's specific concept restarted; it is evidence that a related-but-differently-specified project (P5521) is what actually restarted.
